items.title: Intensive Chemotherapy and Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor in Patients with De Novo BCR::ABL1+ Acute Myeloid Leukemia
items.abstract: Retrospective multicenter analysis of 212 adults with de novo BCR::ABL1-positive AML treated 1999-2024. Adding a BCR-ABL1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor to intensive chemotherapy raised the CR/CRi rate from 68% to 89% and 5-year overall survival from 38.5% to 62.9%, supporting TKI incorporation in this rare WHO/ICC-recognized entity.

items.title: Blinatumomab for Replacing Chemotherapy in Pediatric Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
items.abstract: AIEOP-BFM ALL 2017 randomized children with newly diagnosed high-risk B-cell ALL to two cycles of blinatumomab or two cycles of conventional intensive chemotherapy after consolidation. Replacing chemotherapy with the CD19xCD3 T-cell engager significantly improved event-free survival, establishing a lower-toxicity backbone for high-risk pediatric disease.

items.title: Blinatumomab - A New Standard of Care in Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
items.abstract: NEJM editorial accompanying the AIEOP-BFM ALL 2017 trial, arguing that substituting blinatumomab for intensive chemotherapy blocks is now a standard-of-care option in newly diagnosed pediatric high-risk B-ALL and framing the remaining questions about which patients still need chemotherapy intensity.

items.title: Venetoclax Plus Hypomethylating Agent for 7- Versus 14- Versus 21- Versus 28-Day Cycles in Newly-Diagnosed Acute Myeloid Leukemia
items.abstract: Mayo Clinic series of 540 newly diagnosed AML patients receiving venetoclax plus HMA compared cycle-1 venetoclax durations of 7, 14, 21 and 28 days. Transplant rates and transplant-censored survival were statistically indistinguishable across schedules at 37.7 months median follow-up, with outcome driven by ELN 2024 and Mayo genetic risk rather than venetoclax duration.

items.title: Targeting CD38 with bispecific antibody XmAb 18968 in patients with relapsed/refractory acute myeloid leukemia and T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia
items.abstract: Phase 1 multicenter trial of the CD38xCD3 T-cell engager XmAb18968 in 22 heavily pretreated adults with relapsed/refractory AML or T-ALL. No grade 3 or higher cytokine release syndrome or neurotoxicity occurred, and the Fc-modified design limited non-selective effector activation, establishing CD38 as a tractable engager target outside myeloma.

items.title: Dynamic genetic and nongenetic RAS-pathway activation drives resistance to FLT3 and BCL2 inhibitor therapy
items.abstract: Multiomic single-cell DNA/protein and RNA/protein profiling of AML patients on the phase 1b venetoclax-plus-gilteritinib trial. Although the doublet eliminated FLT3-mutant clones, resistance emerged through genetic and nongenetic RAS-pathway activation and transcriptional state shifts invisible to bulk sequencing.

items.title: Long-term outcomes of azacitidine, venetoclax, and gilteritinib in newly diagnosed FLT3-mutated AML
items.abstract: Phase 2 study of the azacitidine-venetoclax-gilteritinib triplet in 30 unfit adults with newly diagnosed FLT3-mutated AML (median age 71). CR/CRi was 96% and 47% proceeded to allogeneic transplant; at 41.5 months median follow-up 37% had relapsed, most often with loss of the FLT3 mutation.

items.title: IDH3 regulates citrate homeostasis to control metabolic fitness and venetoclax resistance of AML stem cells
items.abstract: The TCA-cycle enzyme IDH3 is enriched in leukemic stem cells relative to healthy hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, and TCA activity tracks with worse AML outcomes. IDH3A knockdown impaired colony formation, organoid growth and engraftment while sparing normal hematopoiesis, and re-sensitized stem cells to venetoclax.

items.title: Type-I interferon-activated NK cells control polycythemia vera in vivo
items.abstract: Interferon alfa works in polycythemia vera at least partly through natural killer cells: IFN-alpha expanded CD27+ NK cells in a transgenic PV mouse model, NK depletion abolished its therapeutic effect, and in PV or essential thrombocythemia patients on IFN-alpha the frequency of CD56bright NK cells correlated with molecular response.

items.title: Myelodysplasia in VEXAS syndrome
items.abstract: Review of the overlap between VEXAS syndrome - a UBA1-driven clonal hematoinflammatory disorder of older men - and myelodysplastic syndrome, covering how progressive marrow failure emerges, how MDS coexisting with VEXAS differs biologically, and how this shapes decisions about hypomethylating agents, JAK inhibition and allogeneic transplant.

items.title: Rapid, reliable, comprehensive and sensitive detection of MDS-defining cytogenetic changes in AML by an optimized panel of 6 FISH probes
items.abstract: Prospective study in 131 patients with suspected AML testing a streamlined 6-probe FISH panel to identify MDS-defining cytogenetic changes for AML-MR classification and CPX-351 eligibility. All six probes were evaluable in 94.7% of cases, cytogenetic abnormalities were found in 45.8%, and peripheral blood performed comparably to marrow with faster turnaround.

items.title: A hemoglobin >120 g/L trends toward improved survival without increasing vascular events in ESA-treated MDS patients
items.abstract: Matched single-center cohort of erythropoiesis-stimulating-agent responders with lower-risk MDS. Patients whose hemoglobin exceeded the mandated 120 g/L ceiling trended toward better overall survival without an excess of cardiovascular events, questioning a threshold extrapolated from solid-tumor thrombosis data.

items.title: AAML1831: A Phase III Trial Comparing Standard Induction Therapy With CPX-351 in De Novo Pediatric AML
items.abstract: Children's Oncology Group phase 3 trial randomizing patients 21 years and younger with newly diagnosed AML to two cycles of liposomal daunorubicin/cytarabine (CPX-351) or standard daunorubicin/cytarabine induction, all with gemtuzumab ozogamicin. CPX-351 did not improve outcomes over conventional induction in this pediatric population.

items.title: Therapeutic targeting of IL-17A-driven PTGS2/NLRP3 inflammasome activation in juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia
items.abstract: In a Shp2E76K JMML mouse model, mutant macrophages upregulated IL-17A to trigger NLRP3 inflammasome and PTGS2 signaling, driving marrow inflammation, regulatory T-cell expansion and T-cell exhaustion. Blocking the axis restored antitumor immunity, offering a non-transplant strategy for PTPN11-mutant disease.

items.title: Mosunetuzumab With Response-Adapted Polatuzumab Vedotin and Obinutuzumab in Untreated Indolent B-Cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma
items.abstract: Chemotherapy-free phase 2 study in 42 untreated follicular or marginal zone lymphoma patients: eight cycles of mosunetuzumab, with polatuzumab vedotin plus obinutuzumab added only for those short of complete response. End-of-treatment ORR was 100% and CR 86%, 2-year PFS 89%, and all cytokine release syndrome was grade 1 with no tocilizumab use.

items.title: A single-cell atlas of large B cell lymphomas reveals distinct malignant archetypes predictive of clinical outcomes
items.abstract: Single-cell RNA, BCR and TCR sequencing across 63 large B-cell lymphoma biopsies identified five conserved malignant transcriptional archetypes that co-occur within individual tumors. High abundance of a quiescent, memory-B-like Archetype 4 predicted poor event-free survival after standard immunochemotherapy.

items.title: LymphGen-Sig: Integrating Genetic and Transcriptional States to Predict Therapeutic Response in Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
items.abstract: LGsig is a gene-expression platform built on subtype-specific signatures from 764 paired genomic-transcriptomic DLBCL cases. Unlike LymphGen, it classifies every tumor and folds in nongenetic biology, improving prediction of therapeutic response and making genetic subtyping usable with a single assay.

items.title: Loncastuximab tesirine in heavily pretreated patients with large B-cell lymphoma: a German Lymphoma Alliance analysis
items.abstract: Real-world analysis of 93 heavily pretreated large B-cell lymphoma patients across 31 German centers, 76% of whom had already received CAR T cells, bispecific antibodies or both. The CD19 antibody-drug conjugate produced a 27% overall and 10% complete response rate with median PFS 2.2 and OS 4.4 months, though responders reached 11.4 months PFS.

items.title: Peripheral CD8+ T-cell clonality and NK-cell expansion mark early response to mosunetuzumab in indolent B-cell lymphoma
items.abstract: Serial immune profiling of patients on fixed-duration subcutaneous mosunetuzumab for untreated follicular or marginal zone lymphoma. By week three, broad cytokine induction, a shift toward transitional effector-memory CD8 T cells, and clonal CD8 expansion with NK-cell recovery marked patients heading for response.

items.title: Age, anthracycline and mortality in 28,000 classic Hodgkin lymphoma patients: cohort study of a complete population
items.abstract: Population-based English registry study of 28,175 classic Hodgkin lymphoma patients diagnosed 1997-2020, focused on 1,958 aged 60-79 with known first-line regimens. All-cause, lymphoma-specific and other-cause mortality were modelled to separate the contributions of age, comorbidity and anthracycline exposure to the well-known survival gap in older patients.

items.title: Outcomes of CHOP, CHOEP or EPOCH in aggressive adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma: an international cohort analysis
items.abstract: International retrospective cohort across five Latin American countries and the United States comparing etoposide-containing regimens with CHOP in acute and lymphomatous adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma diagnosed 2000-2023, using propensity-score weighting to test whether intensification improves response or survival in this HTLV-1-driven disease.

items.title: T-cell lymphoma following chimeric antigen receptor-T therapy: a cause for concern?
items.abstract: Synthesis of pivotal trials, registries, meta-analyses, pharmacovigilance data and molecular case reports on secondary T-cell malignancies after CAR T-cell infusion. Reported incidence is approximately 0.03-0.3%, and the authors weigh biological plausibility against the far larger competing risks these patients face.

items.title: Cytokine concentrations in pediatric primary mediastinal large B cell lymphoma correlate with disease extent and outcome
items.abstract: Plasma profiling of 24 cytokines at diagnosis in a population-based cohort of 62 children with primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma. CCL4, CCL17, IL-6 and the CXCL8-11 axis were elevated versus controls, and CCL17 in particular tracked with disease extent, offering a candidate stratification marker where none currently exists.

items.title: Next-generation antibody-based therapeutics in cancer: antibody-drug conjugates and bispecific antibodies across hematologic malignancies and solid tumors
items.abstract: Wide-angle review of ADCs and bispecific antibodies, from trastuzumab deruxtecan redefining HER2-low disease to newer TROP2, CLDN18.2, B7-H3 and HER3 payload targets, alongside CD20xCD3, BCMAxCD3, GPRC5DxCD3 and CD19xCD3 engagers and the emerging bispecific-ADC constructs.

items.title: T-cell dynamics, CD8/NK ratio and tumor survival hallmarks determine response to T-cell bispecific forimtamig in myeloma
items.abstract: Correlative phase 1 analysis of the GPRC5DxCD3 bispecific forimtamig. A machine-learning model identified the blood and marrow T-to-NK-cell ratio as the strongest predictor of response, while single-cell transcriptomics linked resistance to tumor DNA-repair and proliferation programs rather than T-cell exhaustion.

items.title: PKMYT1 is a targetable vulnerability in del(17p) high-risk multiple myeloma
items.abstract: Integrating patient RNA sequencing with cell-line dependency data nominated the WEE-family kinase PKMYT1 as a synthetic vulnerability in del(17p) myeloma. The selective inhibitor RP-6306 triggered DNA damage and mitotic catastrophe in del(17p) cells while sparing others, and reduced tumor burden in xenograft and TP53-deficient syngeneic models.

items.title: FAERS corroborates the BCMA bispecific PML signal
items.abstract: Pharmacovigilance letter using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System to test a progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy safety signal with BCMA-directed bispecific antibodies in myeloma, adding disproportionality evidence to scattered case reports as these agents move into earlier lines.

items.title: Real-world implementation, feasibility, and early clinical effectiveness of blinatumomab for children with B-ALL in lower middle-income countries
items.abstract: Observational cohort of 106 children with relapsed/refractory or MRD-positive B-ALL treated across six centers in India, Pakistan and Vietnam under a drug-access program. Severe CRS occurred in 2 patients and severe neurotoxicity in 5; 12-month EFS and OS were 58.1% and 82.8%, and MRD negativity after cycle 1 predicted both.

items.title: Association between patient-reported symptoms and clinical outcomes in relapsed/refractory CLL
items.abstract: Patient-reported outcome analysis of the randomized ALPINE trial of zanubrutinib versus ibrutinib in relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL. Zanubrutinib was associated with less recurrent symptomatic deterioration, and worsening on disease-specific symptom scales tracked with shorter progression-free survival and duration of response.

items.title: ASTCT Consensus Grading for Toxicities after Immune Effector Cell Therapy
items.abstract: Updated ASTCT consensus revising the 2019 CRS and ICANS grading scales and, for the first time, defining and grading immune effector cell-associated hematotoxicity, IEC-HS, non-ICANS neurotoxicities such as parkinsonism and cranial nerve palsies, IEC-associated enterocolitis, tumor inflammation-associated neurotoxicity and on-target off-tumor effects.

items.title: Phenotype-directed allele-specific flow cytometry identifies HLA-loss relapse after haploidentical hematopoietic cell transplantation for adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma
items.abstract: Report describing an allele-specific flow cytometry approach that detects loss of the mismatched HLA haplotype at relapse after haploidentical transplant for adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma - the immune-escape mechanism that determines whether donor lymphocyte infusion or a second transplant can work.

items.title: Clinical activity and safety of rilzabrutinib in patients with previously treated immune thrombocytopenia (LUNA3): results from the open-label period of a phase 3 trial
items.abstract: Open-label extension of the 103-center, 24-country phase 3 LUNA3 trial of the reversible BTK inhibitor rilzabrutinib in persistent or chronic immune thrombocytopenia. Durable platelet responses and a favourable safety profile carried through 28 further weeks, including for patients crossing over from placebo.

items.title: FRONTIER5: Safety and patient experience of a direct switch from emicizumab to denecimig (Mim8) in patients with haemophilia A with or without inhibitors
items.abstract: Phase 3b single-arm study switching patients aged 12 and over from emicizumab straight to the next-generation factor VIII-mimetic bispecific denecimig, with no washout and no loading dose, using weekly, fortnightly or monthly pen-injector dosing. Treatment-emergent adverse events and patient-reported experience were the primary focus.

items.title: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Hypersensitivity Reactions after High-dose Intravenous Iron
items.abstract: Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis of randomized trials comparing serious or severe hypersensitivity reaction rates for ferric derisomaltose, ferric carboxymaltose and ferumoxytol in iron-deficiency anemia, giving clinicians comparative risk estimates for a rare but potentially fatal event across modern IV iron formulations.

items.title: Neutrophil-dependent interferonopathy contributes to joint damage in hemophilia
items.abstract: Using factor VIII total-knockout mice and blood from hemophilia A patients with and without active joint bleeding, the authors show that acute hemarthrosis triggers a neutrophil-driven type I interferon response that propagates synovial damage - a mechanism untouched by factor replacement or mimetic prophylaxis.

items.title: Reproductive safety of direct oral anticoagulants after maternal exposure in early pregnancy: a comparative ENTIS cohort study
items.abstract: Multicenter prospective cohort of 343 first-trimester DOAC-exposed pregnancies versus 698 low-molecular-weight-heparin-exposed pregnancies from 2008-2024. DOAC exposure was not associated with increased major birth defects (2.9% vs 4.3%; adjusted OR 0.74), offering reassurance after inadvertent exposure.

items.title: Coagulation Dynamics During Coronary Angiography in Patients Receiving Chronic Direct Oral Anticoagulants: Insights from the Randomized POPular MEASURE Study
items.abstract: Randomized mechanistic study in 120 patients undergoing elective coronary angiography testing whether periprocedural unfractionated heparin can be omitted in those on chronic DOACs. Thrombin generation measured by prothrombin fragment 1+2 was compared against a non-anticoagulated reference cohort receiving heparin.

items.title: Diagnosis and management of subsegmental pulmonary embolism
items.abstract: Case-based review of subsegmental pulmonary embolism, which accounts for 5-10% of PE diagnoses and where the value of anticoagulation remains genuinely unsettled. The authors give evidence-based recommendations where they exist and flag the ongoing randomized trial that should resolve the anticoagulation question.

items.title: Cumulative Stress Measured by Allostatic Load is Associated with Vaso-Occlusive Episodes in Sickle Cell Disease
items.abstract: Allostatic load, a 27-biomarker composite index of multisystem physiological dysregulation, was measured in 129 adults with sickle cell disease. Elevated allostatic load was independently associated with vaso-occlusive episode frequency, giving a quantitative bridge between chronic stress biology and clinical pain crises.

items.title: A Synthetic, Small Molecule, Allosteric Inhibitor of Human Factor XIa for Thrombosis
items.abstract: Discovery and preclinical characterization of SB-01, a highly sulfated aromatic agent that binds both anion-binding exosites of factor XIa to block factor IX activation. SB-01 inhibited rodent arterial and venous thrombosis at 6 and 3 mg/kg respectively, adding an allosteric option to the FXI anticoagulant class.

items.title: Non-Anemic Iron Deficiency in Pregnancy: A Cross-Sectional Study of Prevalence and Predictors
items.abstract: Screening of 201 pregnant individuals at the first obstetric visit found iron deficiency in 59%, of which the large majority (54% of the whole cohort) was non-anemic and would be missed by hemoglobin-based screening. Higher BMI, pagophagia and prior over-the-counter iron use flagged risk.

items.title: Outbreak of Severe Methemoglobinemia during Maritime Migration
items.abstract: Coordinated clinical and toxicologic investigation of clusters of severe acquired methemoglobinemia in migrants arriving at Lampedusa between March 2024 and December 2025. Prolonged dermal contact with fuel-contaminated seawater pooling on overcrowded vessel floors was identified as the cause.

items.title: Tambotatug Pelitecan in Small-Cell Lung Cancer after Platinum-Based Therapy
items.abstract: Phase 3 open-label trial randomizing 451 patients with small-cell lung cancer progressing after first-line platinum to the B7-H3-directed antibody-drug conjugate tambotatug pelitecan or topotecan. The prespecified interim analysis reports overall survival, with progression-free survival and objective response as key secondary endpoints.

items.title: Liquid biopsy for early detection of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
items.abstract: International prospective biomarker study across four countries in 1,785 individuals developing PANXEON, a composite score combining a ten-microRNA exosomal signature with CA 19-9 for early-stage pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma detection - the disease with the least usable blood-based screening to date.

items.title: Trastuzumab Botidotin Versus Trastuzumab Emtansine in HER2-Positive Advanced Breast Cancer: A Phase III, Open-Label, Randomized Controlled Trial
items.abstract: Phase 3 trial at 57 Chinese centers randomizing patients with HER2-positive unresectable or metastatic breast cancer previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane to the novel ADC trastuzumab botidotin or trastuzumab emtansine. The prespecified interim analysis met its progression-free survival endpoint by blinded independent central review.

items.title: Immunotherapy in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma With PD-L1 Combined Positive Score Less Than 1: A Bayesian Meta-Analysis
items.abstract: Bayesian meta-analysis of phase 3 randomized trials reporting the PD-L1 CPS below 1 subgroup in recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. The analysis quantifies the probability that checkpoint inhibitors help or harm a population for whom they are recommended despite thin subgroup evidence.

items.title: PDS0101 With Pembrolizumab in HPV16-Positive Recurrent/Metastatic Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Phase 2 Nonrandomized Clinical Trial
items.abstract: VERSATILE-002 tested the HPV16-targeted therapeutic immunotherapy PDS0101 plus pembrolizumab across 26 centers in the US, UK and Ireland, with separate checkpoint-naive and checkpoint-resistant cohorts, in a population whose incidence is rising and where durable responses remain the minority.

items.title: Circulating Tumor DNA Profiling Defines Risk Classification in Patients With Ewing Sarcoma: A Report From the Children's Oncology Group and the LEOPARD Study
items.abstract: Prospective validation of baseline ctDNA as a prognostic factor in localized and metastatic Ewing sarcoma, embedding ultralow-pass whole-genome and hybrid-capture sequencing into the LEOPARD biology study and the frontline metastatic trial AEWS1221 to build clinical-molecular risk groups.

items.title: Personalized Circulating Tumor DNA Analysis for Predicting Outcomes and Tracking Response to Radiotherapy and Pembrolizumab in Localized Sarcomas: Analysis of the SU2C-SARC032 Trial
items.abstract: Personalized ctDNA assays tracking a median of 46 somatic mutations per patient were applied to 313 plasma samples from 106 patients in the randomized SU2C-SARC032 trial, testing whether low-mutational-burden soft tissue sarcomas can be monitored through preoperative radiotherapy with or without pembrolizumab.

items.title: Pembrolizumab Plus Chemotherapy for Cervical Cancer: An Exploratory Analysis of the KEYNOTE-826 Randomized Clinical Trial
items.abstract: Ad hoc 5-year follow-up of the phase 3 double-blind KEYNOTE-826 trial of pembrolizumab added to platinum chemotherapy with or without bevacizumab in previously untreated persistent, recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer, extending survival and safety beyond the 39-month final analysis.

items.title: Esophageal Cancer
items.abstract: NEJM review of esophageal cancer, the seventh leading cause of cancer death worldwide with population 5-year survival rarely above 20%. Covers the diverging epidemiology of adenocarcinoma and squamous-cell carcinoma and recent developments in screening, perioperative therapy and immunotherapy.

items.title: Identification of broadly tumour-reactive gamma-delta TCRs from multiple myeloma
items.abstract: PreGame, a machine-learning algorithm applied to single-cell CITE sequencing, separates genuinely tumour-reactive gamma-delta T cells from bystanders in multiple myeloma and solid cancers. The recovered TCRs recognized targets broadly across tumors, opening a route to off-the-shelf, HLA-unrestricted cell therapies.

items.title: Latent effector T cells mediate immunotherapy responses in the bone marrow microenvironment
items.abstract: Integrating TCR profiling, HLA immunopeptidomics and functional screening in marrow from myeloma and AML patients, the authors find tumor-reactive T cells defined by a conserved effector program - not the exhaustion phenotype seen in solid tumors - and build TFiT, a classifier that stratifies immunotherapy response.

items.title: Mitochondrial ATP promotes T cell differentiation through chromatin accessibility
items.abstract: D-alpha-hydroxybutyrate acts as a signaling molecule that switches CD8 T cells from glycolysis to fatty-acid-fuelled oxidative phosphorylation, raising phosphocreatine reserves and coupling mitochondrial ATP output to chromatin accessibility at effector genes - a metabolic lever for engineering more durable cytotoxic T cells.

items.title: Evolution and heterogeneity of lethal metastatic bladder cancer subtypes
items.abstract: Rapid-autopsy program profiling terminal metastatic urothelial cancer enriched for histological variants. Metastasis-to-metastasis seeding dominated, polyclonal migration predicted poor prognosis, plasmacytoid tumors uniquely exploited the Fanconi anemia pathway to blunt chemotherapy damage, and post-mortem cell-free DNA recapitulated subtype identity.

items.title: A universal visual foundation model for computational cytopathology
items.abstract: CROWN was pretrained without manual annotation on more than 10 million cytology image patches using a DINOv2 self-supervised framework and evaluated across 202 task-setting combinations spanning classification, segmentation, detection, retrieval and slide-level prediction, outperforming established encoders across public and institutional cohorts.

items.title: Spatial biology reveals altered macrophage states in immunosuppressed non-melanoma skin cancer
items.abstract: Single-cell, spatial transcriptomic, multiplex immunofluorescence and spatial epigenomic profiling of skin cancers in immunocompetent versus systemically immunosuppressed patients - a population that includes transplant recipients. Immune composition was preserved but macrophage density, T-cell clonal diversity and spatial niches were altered.

items.title: A bivalent molecular glue linking lysine acetyltransferases to oncogene-induced cell death
items.abstract: KAT-TCIPs chemically redirect p300/CBP to cell-death genes normally repressed by the DLBCL driver BCL6, reprogramming the epigenome to trigger apoptosis. A crystal structure of the induced p300-BCL6 complex explains the potency and selectivity, and different transcriptional activators produced distinct genomic responses.
